title: Property-(P) resolution of a right DG module over an arbitrary DG algebra
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$; its cohomology is $H^i(M)=\ker(d:M^i\to M^{i+1})/d(M^{i-1})$, and a quasi-isomorphism is a homomorphism of differential graded modules (degree-preserving, $A$-linear, commuting with the differentials) inducing isomorphisms on all $H^i$. For $k\in\mathbf Z$ let $A[k]$ be the shifted module with $A[k]^i=A^{i+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_A$ and right action by multiplication. Say that a right differential graded $A$-module $P$ has property (P) if there is a filtration $0=F_0P\subset F_1P\subset F_2P\subset\cdots$ by differential graded submodules such that $P=\bigcup_{n\geq0}F_nP$, each inclusion $F_nP\subset F_{n+1}P$ admits a left inverse as a map of graded right $A$-modules (not necessarily commuting with $d$), and each quotient $F_{n+1}P/F_nP$ is isomorphic, as a differential graded $A$-module, to a direct sum $\bigoplus_{j\in J_n}A[k_{nj}]$ over a set $J_n$ (possibly empty) with integers $k_{nj}$. Let $A$ and $M$ have their underlying sets in the module universe $u$. Then there exist a right differential graded $A$-module $P$ with property (P), whose underlying sets and index sets $J_n$ lie in $u$, and a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to M$, which may moreover be taken degreewise surjective. No boundedness, countability or commutativity assumption on $A$ or $M$ is imposed; the case $M=0$ is included.

source.place: Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve (statement and proof, via Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient); property (P) as defined in Tag 09KK, section-P-resolutions; admissibility of the inclusions by Tag 09KJ, lemma-target-graded-projective.

proof.text: Set $M_0=M$. Inductively apply [lem-sfb-dg-two-layer-free-cover] to $M_i$, obtaining $\pi_i:Q_i\to M_i$ and its basis sets $U_i,V_i$, and put $M_{i+1}=\ker\pi_i$ with its induced differential and right action. This is a DG submodule since $\pi_i$ commutes with both. Write $j_{i+1}:M_{i+1}\hookrightarrow Q_i$ and $f_{i+1}=j_{i+1}\pi_{i+1}$. Then $f_if_{i+1}=0$ and $\pi_0f_1=0$, since $\pi_i j_{i+1}=0$. Thus the chosen covers give an exact augmented chain $\cdots\to Q_2\to Q_1\to Q_0\to M\to0$ in every degree.

Write $Z^r(T)=\ker(d_T:T^r\to T^{r+1})$. The augmented chain is also exact on $Z^r$ for every $r$. Indeed a cycle $x\in Q_i^r$ in the kernel of the next arrow lies in $M_{i+1}^r$; its differential there is zero because $j_{i+1}$ is injective. Surjectivity on cocycles of $\pi_{i+1}$ lifts $x$ to a cycle in $Q_{i+1}^r$. At the augmented end, surjectivity on cocycles of $\pi_0$ gives $Z^r(Q_0)\to Z^r(M)\to0$. The converse inclusions follow from the vanishing consecutive composites.

Define $P^n=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}Q_i^{n+i}$ with the unchanged right action. For homogeneous $x\in Q_i^b$, of total degree $b-i$, put $D(x)=f_i(x)+(-1)^id_{Q_i}(x)$, omitting $f_0$. Both terms have total degree $b-i+1$. In $D^2$, the pure terms vanish and the mixed terms cancel: their signs are $(-1)^{i-1}$ and $(-1)^i$, while $f_i$ commutes with the internal differentials. The coefficient of $x\,d_A(a)$ in $D(xa)$ is $(-1)^{i+b}=(-1)^{b-i}$, so the DG Leibniz rule holds. Let $q:P\to M$ be $\pi_0$ on $Q_0$ and zero on the other summands. The identity $\pi_0f_1=0$ and the fact that $\pi_0$ is a DG map show that $q$ is a DG map. It is degreewise surjective because $\pi_0$ is.

Forget the DG action and view the augmented chain as complexes of $\mathbf Z$-modules. Steps 1 and 2 verify degreewise exactness and exactness of every augmented cocycle sequence, precisely the hypotheses of [lem-pc-derived-total-resolution-quasi-iso]. Its column $p=-i$ is $Q_i$, so its direct-sum total has differential $f_i+(-1)^id_{Q_i}$ and augmentation $q$. The cited theorem gives isomorphisms $H^n(P)\to H^n(M)$ for every $n$. Thus $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism as defined in the item; forgetting the action did not change cycles or boundaries.

proof.text: Use the bases supplied by [lem-sfb-dg-two-layer-free-cover]. Give $e_u\in Q_i$, $u\in U_i$, height $2i$, and $e_v\in Q_i$, $v\in V_i$, height $2i+1$; their total degree is $t_w-i$. Let $F_nP$ be the graded span of basis vectors of height strictly less than $n$. Then $F_0P=0$. The internal differential of a $U_i$ generator is zero, and that of a $V_i$ generator is in the span of $U_i$; the horizontal differential lands in $Q_{i-1}$, whose heights are at most $2i-1$. Hence $D$ strictly lowers generator heights. The Leibniz rule makes each $F_nP$ a DG submodule. Every element has finite basis support, so these submodules exhaust $P$. Deleting all coordinates of height $n$ is a graded right $A$-linear retraction $F_{n+1}P\to F_nP$. Modulo $F_nP$ a generator $e_w$ of height $n$ is closed, and $D(e_wa)=(-1)^{t_w-i}e_wd_A(a)$. Consequently its summand is $A[i-t_w]$ as a DG module, and $F_{n+1}P/F_nP$ is the direct sum of these shifts. This proves property (P), including its zero initial term.

All kernels are subsets of the preceding $u$-small modules. The cover lemma keeps every $Q_i,U_i,V_i$ in $u$, and $\mathbf N,\mathbf Z\in u$. Countable disjoint unions and sets of finite-support functions over $u$-small sets remain in the Grothendieck universe $u$, so the total module and every height-index set $J_n$ lie in $u$. No step used boundedness or a countability bound on $A$ or $M$. For $M=0$ one may instead choose $P=0$, $q=0\to0$, $F_nP=0$ and all $J_n=\varnothing$.
